verifications.claim: As of late March 2026, 30-year fixed mortgage rates averaged around 6.2% to 6.35%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '30-year fixed-rate mortgage is 6.32%'; R4: '30-year fixed mortgage rate rose ... to 6.22%'; R6: 'Freddie Mac Mar 19 2026 6.22%'; R7: '30-year fixed 6.32%'; R10: '30-year fixed rate mortgage rate rose to 6.22%'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly report late March 2026 rates in the 6.22%-6.32% range, fitting 'around 6.2% to 6.35%' precisely.

verifications.claim: As of late March 2026, 30-year fixed mortgage rates marked a 3-month high
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'climbed this week to its highest level in more than three months'; title: 'Average U.S. long-term mortgage rate rises to 6.22%, highest in more than 3 months'
verifications.reasoning: R10 explicitly states the 6.22% rate in late March 2026 is the highest in more than 3 months.

verifications.claim: 30-year fixed mortgage rates dipped below 6% earlier in 2026
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'three weeks ago, the average rate had dropped to just under 6%'; R2: 'dipping even lower in late February and early March'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm rates dropped below 6% in early 2026, before late March rise.

verifications.claim: 30-year fixed mortgage rates averaged 6.67% a year ago
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'One year ago, the rate averaged 6.67%'; R6: 'YOY Change ... 6.67% -0.37%' (MBA), '6.65% -0.43%' (Freddie)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for average rate one year prior to March 2026.

verifications.claim: In March 2026, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was approximately 6.22% to 6.32%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: March 2026 sources report exact figures of 6.22% and 6.32%, matching the approximate range.

verifications.claim: 30-year fixed mortgage rates increased for several consecutive weeks from under 6% to over 6.2%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6 Freddie: 'Mar 05 6.00%, Mar 12 6.11%, Mar 19 6.22%'; R10: 'dropped to just under 6% ... risen every week'; R7: '6.22% last week to 6.32%'
verifications.reasoning: Weekly Freddie Mac data shows consecutive increases from ~6% to 6.22%, supported by descriptions of recent rises from below 6%.

verifications.claim: As of late March 2026, 30-year VA loans averaged around 5.59%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: '30-year VA: 5.59%' (Zillow data, context late March 2026)
verifications.reasoning: Direct report of 30-year VA average at 5.59% in relevant timeframe.

verifications.claim: Demand for refinancing has dropped due to higher rates
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'refinance applications falling nearly 26% week over week'; R4: 'refinancing dropped sharply due to the higher loan rates'; R10: 'sharp drop in home loan refinancing applications'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly link drop in refinance demand to recent rate increases.

verifications.claim: Some market participants anticipate potential rate cuts later in 2026
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'majority of committee members predict at least one more rate cut before the end of 2026'; R7: 'they still project one cut will come by the end of December'
verifications.reasoning: Fed committee projections explicitly anticipate rate cuts later in 2026.
